questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The best educational apps for young children
Children's screen time and how parents can manage it
Why adults should stop using smartphones at work
How to choose a first phone for a child
questions.why: They discuss worries about children's screen time and hear experts' advice for parents.

questions.q: What do Neil and Becca say about their own phone use?
options: Neil uses his phone too much, but Becca doesn't
Neither of them uses a smartphone
They both feel they spend too much time on their phones
They both only use phones for work
questions.why: Neil says he spends far too much time on his phone, and Becca says she does too.

questions.q: What did Australia do at the end of last year?
options: Banned social media apps for under-16s
Banned smartphones in all schools
Limited adults' screen time
Gave free tablets to children
questions.why: Becca says Australia banned access to social media apps for under 16s.

questions.q: What is Dr Emily Goodacre's view on children and technology?
options: Children should be kept away from technology completely
Children should decide for themselves how to use it
Technology is always good for learning
Adults should think carefully and plan how children use it
questions.why: She says it's not about getting them away from technology but 'being intentional' about how it's used.

questions.q: What kind of products does Emily want to see?
options: Cheaper phones and tablets for large families
Products designed around how children develop
Games that children can play for much longer
Devices that only work for one hour a day
questions.why: She wants products that think about childhood first and how children at different stages develop.

questions.q: What has Dr Becky Kennedy noticed about parents?
options: They don't really care much about screen time
They want the government to solve the problem
They use screens more often than their children
They want to understand it and make small changes
questions.why: She says parents are very eager to understand and want practical, realistic things to make little shifts.

questions.q: What small change does Becky give as an example?
options: Moving the device somewhere the child can't see it
Turning off the internet at night
Letting children use screens only at weekends
Buying a device without games
questions.why: Becca says Becky's example is moving the device somewhere it can't be seen.

questions.q: Why does Becky suggest telling the child why the device was moved?
options: To punish the child for their bad behaviour
To make the child feel guilty about the phone
To show it's hard for anyone to ignore a screen
To teach the child how to hide things from adults
questions.why: She'd explain it's really hard to see a screen and not want to use it: 'I wasn't setting you up for success.'
